extracted.intended_audience: news service managers, journalists, and legal counsel (readers of court affidavits)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational standards, customary practices, and managerial duties for wire/news-service bureaus (collection, verification, distribution, and use of tips), presented in affidavits in litigation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accessing competitor dispatches
rubrics_metrics.description: "they were, under no circumstances whatever, to make any attempt to gain access to or knowledge of The Associated Press despatches ... or to even look at the same."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions were repeatedly given to employees not to attempt to obtain, view, or otherwise access The Associated Press dispatches delivered to rival papers; this was done to avoid imperiling relations with the Associated Press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau Manager supervisory responsibility and exclusive control
rubrics_metrics.description: "To supervise and conduct the business of the defendant at the point where the bureau is located and to supervise and direct the work of the persons employed in connection with the bureau. The Bureau Manager is responsible for and has exclusive control of the collection and distribution of the news of the defendant in the Bureau territory."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bureau manager must oversee all bureau operations, direct staff, and take responsibility for gathering and distributing the service's news within the territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection and transmission duties of Bureau Manager
rubrics_metrics.description: "He should collect news originating in his particular territory and transmit the same to the central office. ... in case of important news which is of country-wide value and interest, to advise the New York office of the character of the story and of the number of words necessary to tell the story."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers are to collect local news, assess its broader value, advise headquarters on significance and length, and transmit full or edited text as directed by central office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local discretion to carry news on local circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the news is of particular interest to clients in the Ohio Circuit ... the Cleveland Bureau Manager, without direction from New York, and using his own judgment, files such news or causes such news to be carried over the Ohio telegraph circuit to the clients and customers of defendant in that circuit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureaus may exercise local judgment to distribute items to regional clients without prior New York approval when relevant to that circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing abbreviated 'pony' reports to immediate clients
rubrics_metrics.description: "entrusted with the duty of supplying, by telephone or telegraph, to clients in immediate touch with his bureau, abbreviated news reports ... he handling this matter to these clients ... in the exercise of his own discretion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers may supply short, immediate updates to nearby clients by phone/telegraph, using discretion about content and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to employ and pay local assistants for gathering local news
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Cleveland Bureau Manager ... is empowered to pay a stated salary to a man selected by him, who is employed in the office of the Cleveland News, and to make an arrangement with such person to assist him in getting whatever local news the Cleveland News might get which would be of interest to the clients of the defendant."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau managers may hire or arrange with local newspaper staff or others to obtain local news; such arrangements can include payment for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation policy for local tip providers (historical example)
rubrics_metrics.description: It was the recollection that managers were authorized "to pay each of the men employed by the Cleveland News, who were employed by defendant's Cleveland Bureau to tip it off as to Cleveland local happenings, at a flat rate of five dollars per week."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small weekly payments (here $5/week historically) were used to compensate local contacts for regular tipping about local happenings; intended purpose was protection and local coverage, not to obtain competitor dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom of newspapers combining reports and cross-checking services
rubrics_metrics.description: "The newspapers ... when preparing an article ... are accustomed ... to combine the matter contained in both such stories. It has been the custom ... to call up the local bureau of defendant and inquire ... what information the defendant has with respect to the same story."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newspapers often integrate material from multiple services and routinely call bureaus to compare or obtain complementary information to produce a single comprehensive article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification effect when a newspaper queries a bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: "when a newspaper taking the news report of both complainant and defendant, calls the local bureau of either news service and asks what information that bureau has as to a certain story ... the local bureau so called is advised at once of the existence of such story and of the fact that the opposition news service is carrying it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A newspaper's inquiry alerts the contacted bureau that a competitor is carrying the item; this is a routine operational consequence of inter-bureau communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification requirement before sending stories based on tips
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have used the tips or suggestions so obtained ... for the purpose of obtaining the full story ... I do not recollect having ever sent out any information to clients of defendant without verification upon the tip or suggestion so received. It was my invariable custom and rule, upon the receipt of such tip or suggestion, to verify it from first-hand information, or from other sources under my control, and if verified, to send the story out to defendant's clients and customers as verified."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tips or suggestions (including those pointing to stories carried by other services) must be independently verified—preferably by first‑hand information or corroborating sources—before distribution to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customary practice: promptly investigate and use tips to obtain stories
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is a well known and I believe practically universal custom for the news services of this country to receive tips of the character which I have outlined, and to promptly investigate them when so received, and by using these tips to obtain information, are enabled to send out the stories to their subscribers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving, investigating, and acting on tips is a standard operational practice among news services to enable timely reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on rewriting or republishing unverified bulletins
rubrics_metrics.description: Message quoted: "Under no circumstances ever put out such bulletin again. We have bureau in Birmingham. Message us only. Do not rewrite anything."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local bureaus should not rewrite or republish unverified bulletins; they should notify central bureaus so headquarters can obtain or verify the story via its own resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity of dispatches received from foreign offices
rubrics_metrics.description: "so far as I know, the defendant has at no time falsified or garbled any of the news matters received from its London office."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News services must not materially change, garble, or falsify dispatches received from their foreign offices; accuracy of transmitted foreign dispatches must be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent foreign sources and payment for cable news
rubrics_metrics.description: The International News Service ... was, in fact, receiving from London and elsewhere in Europe large quantities of news, and for that news was paying large sums of money for cable tolls and maintaining special correspondents at a large cost in London and elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services are expected to secure their own foreign news through paid cable services and maintained correspondents rather than rely exclusively on competitors' foreign reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited responsibility for clients' editorial combinations or headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to the Chicago Examiner story ... 'With the headline, however, the defendant had nothing to do, and was in no sense responsible for it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A news service is not responsible for how a client newspaper edits, combines, or headlines an article produced from supplied dispatches; responsibility is limited to the content transmitted by the service.
